findings.severityNote: Info (critical had the protections been absent)
findings.title: Public input aliasing
findings.description: Public input aliasing. Nullifier n + r is the same field element but a different string in the nullifier set, i.e. a double spend of the same note. Two protections: strict parsing (field < r) and the check in snarkjs 0.7.5

findings.title: mintAmount > 2^63−1 passed validation, but MINT (publicAmount as i64) cannot carry it: the token could never be minted
findings.description: mintAmount > 2^63−1 passed validation, but MINT (publicAmount as i64) cannot carry it: the token could never be minted

findings.title: Merkle root was not verified
findings.description: Merkle root was not verified: the data source (API) could add, remove or alter transactions in a block while keeping a valid header. A duplicate check (CVE-2012-2459) was added as well

findings.title: snarkjs accepts the point at infinity and G2 points outside the subgroup (it only checks that points lie on the curve)
findings.description: snarkjs accepts the point at infinity and G2 points outside the subgroup (it only checks that points lie on the curve). Found while developing the codec

findings.title: Cross-layer invariant
findings.description: Cross-layer invariant. The circuit does not range-check publicAmount; the balance is sound only when |publicAmount| < 2^63. This is currently enforced by the indexer: i64 in the envelope, TRANSACT = 0, MINT = mintAmount
findings.status: documented. Any new operation (unshield) must preserve this invariant

findings.title: Someone else's MINT envelope from the mempool could be copied into one's own transaction with a treasury payment
findings.description: Someone else's MINT envelope from the mempool could be copied into one's own transaction with a treasury payment. The note still went to the original recipient, but if the copy was included in a block first, the original transaction was rejected and its payment was burned
findings.status: fixed: the MINT body contains bindOutpoint, and the indexer requires it to be the first input. Test A-6 + live check on signet. For wallets that select inputs themselves (Unisat), MINT_SCRIPT was added: binding to the payer's scriptPubKey. Test + live check. A mint over the cap still burns the payment — by design, as with Runes

findings.title: Note encryption is not proven in the circuit
findings.description: Note encryption is not proven in the circuit. A sender can send a garbage ciphertext, in which case the recipient will not find the note and the payment is effectively burned. Deliberate trade-off (SPEC §1)

findings.title: build/dev is a single-participant dev setup; zkey verify — OK
findings.description: build/dev is a single-participant dev setup; zkey verify — OK
findings.status: mainnet: public ceremony tooling ready (docs/CEREMONY.md), open until the ceremony runs; signet: DEV setup by design (its genesis pins it)

findings.title: The indexer takes the header chain from the API on trust (does not verify PoW)
findings.description: The indexer takes the header chain from the API on trust (does not verify PoW)
findings.status: partially fixed: headers verified (linkage, proof of work, retarget, MTP, version, checkpoints, most work among what the source serves) in the indexer, CLI and browser replay; receipts check linked or bounded headers; a Bitcoin Core RPC source lets an operator index from their own node; open: a single source can withhold blocks; the signet signature (BIP325) is not checked

findings.title: TRANSACT validity must never depend on its carrier transaction: extDataHash covers only the envelope body
findings.description: TRANSACT validity must never depend on its carrier transaction: extDataHash covers only the envelope body. Any future unshield must put its BTC destination and any relayer fee inside the body bound by extDataHash.
findings.status: documented; relied on by anyone who carries an envelope (copy envelope and the paid relayer)

findings.title: prevoutScript (used by MINT_SCRIPT) now reads raw transaction hex and checks its txid before using the output script, instead of trusting the explorer's JSON
findings.description: prevoutScript (used by MINT_SCRIPT) now reads raw transaction hex and checks its txid before using the output script, instead of trusting the explorer's JSON.

findings.title: A MINT_SCRIPT carried in a coinbase halted every replayer
findings.description: A MINT_SCRIPT carried in a coinbase halted every replayer. The binding check looked up the output spent by the first input, but a coinbase's only input is the null outpoint, which no data source can serve, so the server, the CLI and the browser all retried that block forever. Such a MINT_SCRIPT is now rejected as MINT not bound to this payer with no lookup (SPEC §7). Only block producers can build one; none exists on signet since activation height 324,592, so no past verdict changes. Blocks also apply all or nothing, so a failed lookup never leaves a half-applied block.

findings.title: An envelope handed to anyone (relayer or mempool) stays valid until anchor + 100, because anyone can re-carry it
findings.description: An envelope handed to anyone (relayer or mempool) stays valid until anchor + 100, because anyone can re-carry it. Its notes may only be used to retry that same transfer until then, or until its nullifiers are spent, so a retry can never double-pay.

findings.title: A relayer cannot alter or redirect a transfer and sees no plaintext, but it sees the submitter's IP and timing
findings.description: A relayer cannot alter or redirect a transfer and sees no plaintext, but it sees the submitter's IP and timing. Liveness and censorship by IP are trusted. The free relayer this row first described ("Ghost Relay") is retired, see R-2.
findings.status: documented in the UI and README

findings.title: A sponsored relayer can be drained by anyone
findings.description: A sponsored relayer can be drained by anyone. The free relayer ("Ghost Relay") paid every private transfer's carrier from the operator's own BTC. A zero-value transfer is valid and needs no tokens (an input with inAmount = 0 skips the Merkle check, ForceEqualIfEnabled), so anyone with CPU for proofs could make it pay carrier fees without end. Budget caps, rate limits and the proof-of-work only capped the loss per day and turned it into a denial of service.
findings.status: fixed: the free relayer is retired (stage 0 of docs/design/paid-relay.md); the server refuses to start a relayer without a relay balance configuration, and relaying is paid only from prepaid relay balances, in confirmed BTC credited before carriage (R-3). Test: test/paid-relay-stage0.test.mjs

findings.title: I-PAY: the operator never pays any part of a user's transaction
findings.description: I-PAY: the operator never pays any part of a user's transaction. I0 provenance (assertProvenance), I1 coverage (signPoolTx, the only signing call site, which charges the exact fee before any signature) and I2 books (checkBooks / RelayBooks.checkI2, which halts the relayer on any mismatch).
findings.status: implemented in the relayer; tested in test/relay-books.test.mjs, test/relay-balance-relayer.test.mjs, test/relay-account.test.mjs, test/relay-balance-cli.test.mjs and end to end in test/relay-balance-e2e.test.mjs
